- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at +3–4 points above peak for next 3–5 days.
- In 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust — force a 1–2 day lagged correction downward.
- Model ignores sentiment momentum: if sentiment is trending upward, forecast should not be flat — add 0.1–0.3% per day to forecast if sentiment >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >+2% per week), model often lags — add 0.2–0.5% per week to forecast if sentiment is positive and price is rising.
